document.title: Foundations of Public Health Communication
document.summary: This lecture explains how audience, message design, and delivery channels shape effective public health communication.

blocks.text: Public health communication translates evidence into messages that people can understand and use. Its purpose is not only to transfer information, but also to support informed decisions.

blocks.title: Key definition
blocks.text: A target audience is the specific group a message is designed to reach and influence.

items: What should they understand or do?
Which channel can reach them effectively?

blocks.text: Effective messages are accurate, focused, actionable, and appropriate for the audience's language and context.

rows: Use direct language and explain unfamiliar terms.
Connect the message to the audience's needs.
State the next step people can take.

blocks.title: Remember
blocks.text: Do not add certainty that is not present in the evidence. Communicate limits and uncertainty honestly.
